activities.instructions: Ayuda a la rana a cruzar el río eligiendo el nenúfar correcto en cada salto.
activities.prompt: Partida de 8 rondas para repasar el tema jugando.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence uses the past simple correctly?

options.text: They going yesterday.
They gone yesterday.
They went yesterday.

rounds.explanation: The irregular past of «go» is «went».

options.text: She has worked here for three years.
She works here for three years.
She has worked here since three years.

rounds.explanation: A duration such as «three years» takes «for».

options.text: She explained to me the rule.
She explained the rule to me.
She explained me the rule.

rounds.explanation: «Explain» takes the thing directly and the person after «to».

options.text: Mia told that she was busy.
Mia said that she was busy.
Mia said me that she was busy.

rounds.explanation: Use «said that» without a direct person object.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence uses a preposition correctly?

options.text: We arrived in the station.
We arrived at the station.
We arrived on the station.

rounds.explanation: The usual phrase is «arrive at the station».

options.text: The form was signing yesterday.
The form was signed yesterday.
The form is signed yesterday.

rounds.explanation: The past passive is «was signed».

options.text: No sooner had we arrived than it started raining.
No sooner we had arrived than it started raining.
No sooner had we arrived when it started raining.

rounds.explanation: The fixed pattern is «no sooner had ... than ...».

options.text: The tunnel is believed be safe.
The tunnel is believed to be safe.
The tunnel believed to be safe.

rounds.explanation: The reporting passive requires «is believed to be».

activities.explanation: Al terminar la partida verás la media de aciertos y la explicación de cada ronda fallada.

activities.instructions: Colócate en el carril de la respuesta correcta antes de cruzar cada puerta.
activities.prompt: Partida de 8 rondas para repasar el tema jugando.

options.text: Did she goes home?
Did she going home?
Did she go home?

rounds.explanation: After «did», use the base form «go».

rounds.prompt: Which sentence uses a countable noun correctly?

options.text: There are many cars.
There are much cars.
There are a cars.

rounds.explanation: «Cars» is plural countable, so use «many» and «there are».

options.text: If I have time, I would joined.
If I would have time, I join.
If I had time, I would join.

rounds.explanation: The second conditional uses «if + past simple» and «would + base verb».

options.text: She walking to work.
She walk to work.
She walks to work.

rounds.explanation: «She walks» has the correct third-person singular form.

options.text: Do you know where the post office?
Do you know where the post office is?
Do you know where is the post office?

rounds.explanation: The indirect question uses statement order: «where the post office is».

rounds.prompt: Which sentence reports a future plan correctly?

options.text: He said me he would call the next day.
He told that he would call tomorrow.
He said that he would call the next day.

rounds.explanation: The correct sequence is «said that + would call + the next day».

rounds.prompt: Which sentence uses «look forward to» correctly?

options.text: I look forward meeting you.
I look forward to met you.
I look forward to meeting you.

rounds.explanation: The preposition «to» is followed by the gerund «meeting».

options.text: Despite the train was late, we caught it.
Despite the delay, we caught the train.
Despite of the delay, we caught the train.

rounds.explanation: «Despite» can be followed by the noun phrase «the delay» without «of».

activities.explanation: Al terminar la partida verás la media de aciertos y la explicación de cada ronda fallada.

activities.instructions: Apila los fragmentos en orden para levantar la frase.
activities.prompt: Partida de 8 rondas para repasar el tema jugando.

options.text: He doesn't drives.
He not drive.
He doesn't drive.

rounds.explanation: «Doesn't» is followed by the base form «drive».

options.text: The form must be sign today.
The form must signed today.
The form must be signed today.

rounds.explanation: A modal passive is «must + be + past participle»: «must be signed».

rounds.prompt: Which indirect question reports a past action correctly?

options.text: She asked where I had left it.
She asked where I leave had it.
She asked where had I left it.

rounds.explanation: Indirect questions use statement order and past perfect for the earlier action.

options.text: The figures are consistent with the report.
The figures are consistent to the report.
The figures consistent with the report.

rounds.explanation: The collocation is «consistent with».

rounds.prompt: Which sentence uses an article correctly?

options.text: I saw a dogs.
I saw dog.
I saw a dog.

rounds.explanation: The singular countable noun «dog» takes «a» before its consonant sound.

options.text: Although of raining, we walked.
Although the rain, we walked.
Although it was raining, we walked.

rounds.explanation: «Although» introduces a complete clause with a subject and verb.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence uses present perfect correctly?

options.text: I lived here since 2020.
I live here since 2020.
I have lived here since 2020.

rounds.explanation: A starting year takes «since» with present perfect.

options.text: It was such a useful book that I kept it.
It was such useful that I kept it.
It such was a useful book that I kept it.

rounds.explanation: The pattern is «such + a/an + adjective + singular noun».
